title: Rights groups press lawmakers to scrap provision to merge US and Israeli militaries
summary:
Rights groups press lawmakers to scrap provision to merge US and Israeli militaries

On Thursday, 56 civil rights and advocacy groups urged Congress to scrap a defence bill provision that would strengthen US-Israeli military technology ties, according to a letter seen by Reuters. 

Section 219 of the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) intends to institute frameworks for joint ventures, licensing agreements and US-based co-production partnerships. It passed in the House of Representatives in July and is pending Senate approval. 

Thursday’s letter addressed leaders of the House and Senate Armed Services Committees. 

Reuters reported that some of the letter's signatories include Amnesty International and the National Lawyers Guild, as well as Arab and Jewish groups.

“At a time in which American interests are increasingly diverging from those of Israel, and American public opinion is turning increasingly against unconditional support to Israel, creating new points of influence for Israel in the US defense-technology ecosystem is exceptionally dangerous,” read the letter. 

Read more: Rights groups press lawmakers to scrap provision to merge US and Israeli militaries

title: Iran says oil industry circumventing US blockade
summary:
Iran says oil industry circumventing US blockade

Iran’s oil industry continues to find ways around a US military blockade of the country’s ports and vessels, Petroleum Minister Mohsen Paknejad told the Iranian Students News Agency (ISNA).

“We are pursuing various strategies and have taken measures to overcome the blockade,” Paknejad said, describing the situation as difficult.

He said US forces had attacked Kharg Island off Iran’s southwestern coast “more than 550 times” during the first 40 days of the conflict. Iran exported about 90 percent of its crude oil from the island before the war.

title: UN says Israel must withdraw from occupied West Bank
summary:
UN says Israel must withdraw from occupied West Bank

The United Nations Human Rights Office for Palestine said Israel must “end its unlawful presence and evacuate all settlers from the occupied West Bank” following the killing of two Palestinian teenagers on Wednesday in the village of al-Mughayyir.

In a post on X, the agency said the settler and state violence against the people in al-Mughayyir have led to the “complete displacement of Palestinians” in the area, calling Israel to “fulfill its obligation under international law”.

Surrounded by settler outposts, al-Mughayyir has been a target for incessant settler and state efforts to force Palestinian residents to leave. This included more than 50 settler attacks in 2026 alone, according to UN data.

Israeli forces shot and killed two Palestinian boys,16-year-old Khalil Shihadeh and 17-year-old Omar Al Nassaan, in Al Mughayyir during a reported settler attack. Israeli forces and settlers have now killed 9 Palestinians in the town since December 2024, including 5 boys.…

title: Vance: US investigating strike on Iran wedding 'very fully'
summary:
Vance: US investigating strike on Iran wedding 'very fully'

Submitted by Yasmine El-Sabawi on Thu, 09/03/2026 - 20:18
The US vice president insisted that there is no ongoing 'war' with Iran
US Vice President JD Vance take questions from reporters at the White House in Washington, on 3 September 2026 (Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters)
Off

US Vice President JD Vance told reporters on Thursday that the US is "very fully" investigating the military's reported strikes on a wedding in Iran which killed at least four people this week. 

There were at least a dozen other victims along the southern coast of Iran after the US unleashed a barrage of attacks in one of the largest flare-ups since the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding was signed between the two sides more than two months ago. 

"I've been briefed to the extent that I know that we're investigating," Vance said during the White House briefing.

"I will say that the Iranian state media has not been a very good scribe about what's happened in the conflict thus far. So I'm extremely sceptical of this," he added.

"The United States never targets civilians in combat. We never will do that. We never have done that. And unfortunately, obviously, sometimes things happen... When our military makes mistakes, they learn from them to try to get better from them. So we're investigating it very fully."

Vance effectively acknowledged that there are currently no open diplomatic channels between Washington and Tehran when he didn't push back on reporters who contextualised the issue. The vice president had previously led the US negotiating team in both Islamabad and Lucerne.

He did, however, push back on reporters who referred to the ongoing "war". 

"Major combat operations are currently not ongoing, and they haven't been ongoing in a very long time," he said. 

"I wouldn't call it a war. Right now, there is no active shooting."

'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran
Read More »

Yet the vice president spent much of the nearly hour-long briefing explaining that the US must use its military might in the Strait of Hormuz "because the Iranians are shooting at commercial shipping". 

Iran has imposed a blockade - its most effective leverage - on US and Israel-linked vessels in the critical waterway since the early days of the US and Israeli attacks, which began on 28 February.

"Obviously that means some ships don't want to go through [but] we got about 15 million barrels out of the Strait of Hormuz just yesterday, despite the fact that the Iranians continue to shoot," he said.

The US navy imposed a counter-blockade in April. 

"What has anybody in the world done? Why is it incumbent upon the United States of America to be the only country in the world that can actually ensure world energy markets continue to stay supplied?" Vance asked.

He inadvertently answered his own question just minutes later. 

"We are the only country in the world that can ensure, as you heard the president say, the control over the Strait of Hormuz... if we don't do it, nobody else would do it."

'Stop acting like crazy people'

Vance said he has one piece of advice to Iran: "Stop acting like crazy people."

Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref on Thursday said the US has transformed Tehran’s security and defence calculations, warning that Iran will deliver an "asymmetrical" and "multi-layered" response.

Iran's responses have frequently involved targeting US assets in the region, particularly in Kuwait, the UAE, Bahrain, and Jordan. 

"The Americans should start thinking about stockpiling gasoline and fuel. Dark months await the American economy," Aref wrote on X.

"We really have two options here," Vance told reporters. "We could leave, and the entire world would be way worse off because there would be no guaranteed access to oil and gas... or we could accept the Iranians are going to shoot at ships like crazy people, and we're going to do what we have to do in order to ensure that their efforts don't lead to a worldwide energy crisis."

'I don’t think we are ever going to move back into those [Gulf] bases'

- Harrison Mann, former US Defense Intelligence Agency officer

He added that Gulf nations have communicated to Washington that it "would be the worst thing in the world" if the US permanently withdrew from regional bases that have grown exponentially since the 1990 Gulf War.

But it's unclear if forces and civilian personnel evacuated earlier this year will move back. The US has lost 18 military personnel since it launched the war.

"I don't think we are ever going to move back into those bases in Bahrain and Qatar, in Kuwait, in eastern Saudi Arabia," Harrison Mann, a former US Defense Intelligence Agency officer, told a panel hosted by Democracy in the Arab World Now (Dawn) on Thursday.

"This war has made those bases even more of a political liability for the monarchies there," he said, adding that there is a likelihood the US could consolidate its regional military presence in Israel.

That may be an even greater liability, he noted, given Iran-backed groups like Hezbollah in Lebanon have rockets within reach of Israel.

The escalation game

Vance made it clear there is no timeline for an end to hostilities, despite the administration previously pledging to Americans that gasoline prices would drop significantly by the first week of September. That has not materialised.

The US, Vance said, does not plan to "depend on the Iranians behaving responsibly or negotiating in good faith".

"What we're going to do is use the tools that we have at our disposal to ensure that the American people, one, never have to deal with the threat of an Iranian nuclear programme, and two, that world energy markets are properly supplied."

Iran strikes US bases across region after American attack kills 18, including children
Read More »

Negar Mortazavi, a senior non-resident fellow at the Center for International Policy, told the Dawn panel that Iran has learned not to submit to a ceasefire agreement too soon.

In June 2025, when Israel launched its attack on Iran, "they let the war end too soon, within 12 days. They accepted the ceasefire very rushed, and that's why the war came back even more for a third time, which is this year in February," she said.

"And so now the shift in policy or that doctrine is that they have to be more offensive, more aggressive."

"Tehran has learned from dealing with President Trump," Mortazavi added.

"What they keep saying publicly and also privately is that with him, when you back off, he escalates more. If you escalate at some point, he backs off, and they have examples for that."

'Operation economic outcast'

One of the tools in the US toolkit is an expansion of the longstanding sanctions package on Iran, which was unveiled by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent last week. 

"Operation Economic Outcast" is meant to "asphyxiate" Tehran by cutting off its "enablers", he said, adding that President Donald Trump has been speaking to allies around the world about joining the project.

But no leaders were identified nor a timeline divulged.

On Thursday, Vance was asked which countries had stepped up beyond the UAE.

"If you look at Turkey, if you look at Azerbaijan... Saudi Arabia, Qatar, a lot of the Gulf Arab coalition... all across the world, we're actually seeing a lot of countries. Sometimes they're not willing to say so publicly," he said.

When pressed on China - Iran's most powerful ally that has long aided it in evading the US-dominated international financial system - Vance appeared to soften his approach.

"We've certainly had a number of conversations with the Chinese, and frankly, I think the Chinese have been responsive to some of the requests that we've made," he said.

"Say what you will about them; they are not the sort of nation that shoots at commercial shipping because they're not getting their way in an international dispute," he added. "They are, in that way, I think, willing to be a little bit more responsible."

Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to make a state visit to the US later this month.

title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
summary:
Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever.

In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses."

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

summary: يكشف تدقيق في إفصاحات صناديق التقاعد وشركات التأمين حول العالم عن خطر متزايد يواجه الدولار الأميركي: بعض أكبر حائزي الأصول الأميركية باتوا يمتلكون مستويات محدودة من الحماية ضد تراجع العملة، ما قد يجعل الدولار أكثر عرضة لهبوط حاد إذا تغيرت معنويات المستثمرين فجأة.

title: قانون تاريخي في البرازيل لتنظيم استغلال المعادن النادرة
summary: أقرّ مجلس الشيوخ البرازيلي قانونا تاريخيا لتنظيم استكشاف واستغلال المعادن النادرة والاستراتيجية، في خطوة لتعزيز الاستفادة من احتياطيات البلاد الضخمة من الثروة الباطنية.

title: وسط الخلافات.. كندا تؤكد استعدادها لاتفاق تجاري مع أمريكا
summary: قال رئيس الوزراء الكندي مارك كارني، الخميس، إن بلاده مستعدة لإبرام اتفاق تجاري مع الولايات المتحدة يحقق مصالح الطرفين، مؤكدا أن أي اتفاق يجب أن يتسم بالاستقرار والمصداقية.

title: بعد يوم من زيارة شي.. مصر والصين توقعان 20 وثيقة للتعاون باستثمارات ضخمة
summary: وقعت مصر والصين اليوم الخميس، مذكرة تفاهم لإنشاء مجمع صناعي متكامل لإنتاج إطارات السيارات، باستثمارات تصل إلى نحو ملياري دولار.

title: مدفيديف: العقوبات الألمانية ضد روسيا ستلحق أضرارا بالغة باقتصاد ألمانيا وسكانها
summary: حذّر نائب رئيس مجلس الأمن الروسي دميتري مدفيديف من تداعيات العقوبات التي أقرتها الحكومة الألمانية ضد روسيا، مؤكدا أنها ستنعكس سلبا على اقتصاد ألمانيا وسكانها.

title: فيديو.. سقوط الطفل أيوب في بئر ضيقة يحبس أنفاس الجزائر

title: فاتورة الحر القاتلة.. 16300 وفاة في ألمانيا
summary: سجلت ألمانيا عددا غير مسبوق من الوفيات المرتبطة بالحرارة، بلغ 16300 حالة، خلال موجات الحر الشديدة التي اجتاحت أوروبا هذا الصيف، وفقا لبيانات رسمية صدرت الخميس.

title: بمولود جديد.. صلاح يكمل "هاتريك" خارج الملعب
summary: استقبل النجم المصري محمد صلاح طفله الثالث، حسبما أعلن رئيس نادي طرابزون سبور التركي وشقيقة اللاعب على "فيسبوك"، الخميس.

title: مذكرة توقيف جديدة بحق "دكتور فود" بتهمة السرقة في لبنان
summary: أفادت وسائل إعلام لبنانية بأن قاضية التحقيق في جبل لبنان جويل عيسى الخوري، أصدرت مذكرة توقيف وجاهية بحق صانع المحتوى جورج ديب، المعروف باسم "دكتور فود"، بجرم السرقة، في تطور قضائي جديد يضاف إلى ملفاته أمام القضاء اللبناني.

title: نتنياهو يقول إن إسقاط النظام الإيراني "في المتناول" وواشنطن تحقق في ضربة حفل الزفاف
summary: رئيس الوزراء الإسرائيلي بنيامين نتنياهو، قال الخميس، إن إسقاط النظام الجمهورية الإسلامية في إيران "في المتناول"، معتبراً أنها باتت "أضعف" من أي وقت مضى، فيما توعد قائد الحرس الثوري الإيراني  بالثأر.

title: بعد الإفراج عن أحدهم، ماذا نعرف عن المحتجزين اللبنانيين في إسرائيل؟
summary: تسلم لبنان يوم الخميس، أحد المواطنين الذين احتجزتهم إسرائيل لديها، فيما يتبقى أربعة آخرين تأجل الإفراج عنهم، بعدما تبيّن لها أنهم مدنيون لم يشاركوا في أي عمليات ضدها.

summary: كشفت شهادة طبية عسكرية عن فضيحة في حقبة الرئيس الأمريكي السابق جو بايدن، تؤكد وفاة جنود أمريكيين جراء اللقاح الإلزامي الخاص بوباء "كوفيد"، في إطار تحقيق رسمي.

title: عمدة موسكو: الدفاعات الروسية تسقط 10 مسيرات كانت تتجه نحو العاصمة
summary: أعلن عمدة مدينة موسكو سيرغي سوبيانين عن تصدي الدفاعات الجوية الروسية لهجوم بـ10 طائرات مسيرة مشيرا إلى أن المتخصصين يعملون في موقع سقوط الحطام.

title: إيران تكشف عن "وثيقة قطرية" حول حصر الضربات في أهداف عسكرية أمريكية
summary: أكد المتحدث باسم الخارجية الإيرانية اسماعيل بقائي حصر الضربات في أهداف عسكرية أمريكية في قطر، مستندا في ذلك إلى وثيقة قال إنها قطرية وتثبت عدم استهداف طهران لأي مناطق مدنية.

title: 4 ميداليات في اليوم الأول.. انطلاقة قوية لروسيا في بطولة أوروبا للجودو للشباب
summary: حصد الرياضيون الروس أربع ميداليات متنوعة في اليوم الأول من منافسات بطولة أوروبا للجودو للشباب (فئة تحت 21 عاما)، المقامة حاليا في مدينة بودغوريتسا عاصمة الجبل الأسود.

title: US military says 87 vessels diverted so far in Strait of Hormuz
summary:
US military says 87 vessels diverted so far in Strait of Hormuz

US Central Command (Centcom) said it has redirected a total of 87 vessels in the Strait of Hormuz amid the naval blockade of Iran.

Centcom also said in its update that it has disabled three ships so far and boarded another two to ensure “total compliance” with the blockade.

title: Christian village of Taybeh plans US lawsuit over Israeli settler attacks
summary:
Christian village of Taybeh plans US lawsuit over Israeli settler attacks

The municipality of Taybeh, a Christian village in the occupied West Bank, has called on residents who hold US passports or green cards to document attacks and property damage by Israeli settlers ahead of a planned civil lawsuit in the United States.

The municipality said the case would target the settlers and “the American institutions that support these assaults”, adding that the Palestinian-American Olive Branch Funding Group, represented by lawyer Jonathan Kuttab, was prepared to cover the full cost of the case.

title: Israeli attack injures two Palestinian children in occupied West Bank
summary:
Israeli attack injures two Palestinian children in occupied West Bank

Israeli forces shot and injured two Palestinian children in Beit Fajjar, south of Bethlehem, the Wafa news agency reported.

The children were wounded when Israeli forces opened fire with live ammunition during a raid on the town, the report said.

title: Vance says US probing air strike on wedding party in Iran
summary:
Vance says US probing air strike on wedding party in Iran

US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday said the United States is investigating an air strike that Iran says struck a wedding party in Iran.

"We're investigating it because obviously we care. We want to know," Vance told reporters during a White House press briefing.

Iranian officials say four people died and nearly 70 were wounded by a strike that hit a home during a wedding. Iranian state TV reported on Thursday that a fifth person, a 22-year-old woman, had since died in hospital.
